chunks: Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara and Al-Fudayl, said:

We said to him, 'Are the prayers in congregation an obligation?' So he said, 'The prayers are an obligation, and the gathering is not an obligation in all of the prayers, but it is a Sunnah, and whoever leaves it out of preference for it and for the congregation of the believers without an excuse, then there is no prayer for him.'

key_terms.الصَّلَوَاتُ: The prayers (specifically the five daily obligatory prayers)
key_terms.رَغْبَةً: Preference/Desire (doing something out of liking or choosing it over duty)
key_terms.عِلَّةٍ: Excuse/Valid reason (such as illness, fear, etc.)

ai.seo_question: Is praying in congregation obligatory or a Sunnah in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between the individual obligation of prayer and the communal recommendation of congregation, a nuance central to Shia fiqh regarding the validity of solitary prayer. The Imam emphasizes that while congregation is not strictly mandatory for every single prayer, deliberately abandoning it without a valid excuse constitutes a neglect of the community bond, thereby rendering the prayer ineffective. This highlights the Shia view that jamāʿah is a highly emphasized Sunnah with significant spiritual and social weight, rather than a strict condition for the validity of the prayer itself.
